problems.title: Delivery stream re-sends unacked backlog on every write
problems.notes: Phase 2 (W4 step 5): ClientSession keeps lastSentDeliverySeq; live pushes chain from it (base = lastSent) and carry only new operations. The stream rewinds to lastAcked only on a retransmit timeout: an RFC 6298-style RTO from per-batch ack round trips (Karn: no samples from re-sent ranges; floor 1 s, initial 2 s), doubled per re-send and kept until a fresh sample, capped at 5 min; the delivery poll is a safety net with the same window. No client gap report exists yet (engine side), so a dropped batch is recovered after the RTO. Measured with the repro: initial-sync write amplification 2.00x -> 1.00x, steady writes at 20 ms RTT 2.34x -> 1.00x. Unit tests: session/delivery-cursor-liveness.test.ts.

problems.title: Postgres per-instance vector cache; dedup race; INTEGER overflow
problems.notes: Phase 2 (W10 step 1): PostgresServerStore.applyRemoteOperation takes the delivery-counter lock first, then INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING RETURNING; a duplicate rolls back (no delivery seq burned, no cascade). New ServerStore.readVersionVector() reads sync_state; sessions use it at handshake and for the legacy delta (repro test 1 now awaits readVersionVector(): the synchronous getVersionVector() can only reflect the instance's own writes). sequence_number and max_sequence_number migrate to BIGINT once at startup (information_schema-guarded ALTER, under the ensure-tables advisory lock; rewrites the table under an exclusive lock, so expect a pause proportional to log size on first start). sequenceNumber is validated as a safe positive integer on every ingest path (INVALID_SEQUENCE_NUMBER). Tests: store/ingest-integrity.test.ts (Postgres part with KORA_PG_TEST_URL).

problems.title: Delivery stream buffers the whole backlog in memory
problems.notes: Phase 2 (W4 step 6): the delivery stream is filtered and sent per scan chunk (batchSize*5) with a one-batch lookahead for isFinal, so a stream holds at most one chunk plus two batches; the handshake stream runs on the delivery chain after the response (acks and uploads keep flowing) and pauses while the transport reports more than deliveryHighWaterBytes (1 MiB) queued. MemoryServerStore seeks by binary search. LMS #11: records the visibility decisions need are prefetched once per chunk and collection (new optional ServerStore.findRecordsByIds: Postgres/SQLite IN (...), memory map). The handshake vector of a delivery client is the full vector when unscoped and, when scoped, the nodes a metadata pre-pass finds visible (RT-7 kept; the client still needs those entries for its pending count). Repro: 5000 ops scanned before the first send -> 500.

app.transaction reuses sequence numbers; later writes never uploaded
problems.notes: W6: one local write path. Transaction entries are buffered as intent and written at commit inside the commit's storage transaction through the same builders as single-record writes (mutations/write-ops.ts); every sequence number is reserved through that transaction (UPSERT ... RETURNING) and each op is built only after its number is reserved. TransactionSequenceAllocator and the out-of-transaction allocator are removed; remote applies write the vector with MAX. A repair migration re-sequences beta.12 duplicates and a UNIQUE (node_id, sequence_number) index is created on every op table. Earlier: S1 counter stopgap: ApplyPipeline.commitTransaction writes _kora_version_vector as MAX(existing, highest own seq in batch) inside the commit transaction, so later writes no longer reuse sequence numbers or look synced. Concurrent app.transaction calls can still share sequence numbers (repro 'two concurrent app.transaction calls' still fails) until W6 block reservation.

problems.title: Backup restore corrupts timestamps and copies device identity
problems.notes: FIXED (Phase 3, W8b step 1). Backup format version 2 (BACKUP_VERSION 2): canonical Operation NDJSON in HLC order (incl. atomicOps, transactionId, mutationName, fieldVersions, and ops kept only in _kora_seq_conflicts), raw rows incl. tombstones (bytes base64-tagged), version vector, terminal rejections; no _kora_meta at all. Read inside one transaction. Import parses and verifies every op through the canonical serializer (BackupFormatError). Merge mode: every op through the remote-apply path (app.importBackup passes the ApplyPipeline sync uses), vector by MAX, terminal markers added, node_id/node tokens/local nodes/principal bindings/watermarks/acked prefixes never imported. Replace mode (backup/restore.ts): one transaction wipes the target collections and loads ops + rows, keeps node id, tokens, local node registry, principal bindings, acked prefixes; own counters never move backwards; unacknowledged writes of an accepted node are always re-applied on top, other unsynced own writes when keepUnsyncedWrites (default true at store level; app.importBackup defaults it to whether sync is configured and refuses false with sync); a never-accepted node whose writes are dropped restarts its counter after the highest restored number (contiguous); delivery watermarks reset to 0, delta cursor dropped; dropped ops leave the outbound queue. Then Store.reloadFromDisk() (node id, vector, sequence counter, clock advanced past the newest logged timestamp, fresh causal tracker, every subscription invalidated). app.importBackup pauses sync for a replace and resumes it. Version-1 files are refused with BACKUP_FORMAT_OUTDATED; convertBackupV1(data, { dropUnrecoverable }) converts them (drops meta, recovers misread timestamps, decodes bytes). Breaking: restoreBackup(adapter, ...) is deprecated and now opens a temporary Store on the adapter (closing it). Tests: store backup/backup.test.ts, kora import-backup.test.ts. Docs: guide/backup-restore.md. Server backups (server-backup.ts) already used canonical Operation JSON and are unchanged.

problems.title: No log-integrity check: rows damaged by beta.12 backup restore (JSON timestamps read as wallTime NaN/null) or unreadable rows are folded as-is, and compaction gaps are invisible; W7 re-materialization would bake the damage in
problems.notes: W8 step 0 (prerequisite for W7, plan section 3 dependency rules). Store.verifyLogIntegrity({ mode, repair }) runs the full scan and returns a LogIntegrityReport (clean, repaired, newlyQuarantined, quarantined, gaps in this database own nodes below their highest stored sequence, compactedAt). problems.title: Blob chunk requests/responses relayed across tenants; central store serves any hash to any session
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team review 2026-10-01 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1.md). Fixed: BlobAccessIndex (server/src/richtext/blob-access-index.ts) answers whether a live record in a download scope references a hash (BlobRef.hash, manifestHash, or a chunk of a manifest read from the central store or learned from relay-verified bytes); scoped query over blob collections, cached per scope, invalidated on every local write / delivery-log advance / 5 s TTL (cost O(records in scope with blobs) per rebuild; a store hash index is the follow-up). BlobChunkRelay takes a BlobAccessPolicy: central store serves only requesters whose scope references the hash; requests are forwarded only to peers with the same download scope (partition key) or, across scopes, when both reference the hash; responses accepted only from asked peers and only when bytes hash to the requested hash; otherwise bytes:null. Policy errors fail closed.

problems.title: HTTP long-poll: clientId alone binds a request to an authenticated session (session hijack)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team review 2026-10-01 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1.md). Fixed: HttpSyncRequest drops clientId, gains sessionId (x-kora-session) and authorization. The handshake POST opens a session and the 202 returns a server-issued 256-bit id; unknown ids are 404. With auth, every request is authenticated and must match user+device+anonymity of the opener and of the handshake principal (401/403; mismatch ends the session). HTTP sessions idle for httpSessionIdleTimeoutMs (default 2 min) close. HttpLongPollingTransport polls only after the id is issued, sends id + bearer on every request, serializes POSTs, closes on 401/403/404/410. Integration test: tests/integration/http-long-poll.test.ts.

problems.title: Cascade side-effect ops not re-authorized; restrict check counts other tenants' children
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team review 2026-10-01 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1.md). Fixed: applyServerOperation authorizeSideEffect: every cascade/set-null of an untrusted delete is checked against the writer uplink scope (child stored row) before the delete applies; any refusal rejects the whole delete. Decision: integrity judges ALL children in every tenant, but untrusted writers get one generic RESTRICTED rejection (no ids, no counts) for both restrict violations and unauthorized side effects; trusted server deletes keep REFERENTIAL_INTEGRITY. Wired in ClientSession and scoped route-context apply (conditional apply path has no referential side effects).

problems.title: Blob reference forging: writing a record that references a foreign hash grants read access (hash acts as capability)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: a blob reference is authorized at ingest (sync uploads, scoped routes incl. the store conditional path) by BlobAccessIndex.authorizeReference: allowed when the stored record already referenced it, a live record in the writer DOWNLINK scope references it, the writer owns it (pushed the bytes = proof of possession), or nobody references/owns/stores it (atomic first claim). Ownership persisted in blob_owners (memory/SQLite/Postgres; claimBlobIfUnowned atomic, Postgres via advisory xact lock). A chunked reference is readable by its manifestHash only (the whole-blob hash grants nothing). Manifest pushes are refused (BLOB_REFERENCE_FORBIDDEN) unless the pusher may reference every listed chunk; an owned chunk is reachable only via a manifest sharing an owner. Anonymous sessions are their own blob partition (getBlobPartitionKey). Client now uploads blob bytes BEFORE the referencing batch (SyncEngine.setOutboundPreparer; pushes allowed while syncing). Documented: a content hash is not a secret (docs/guide/production-server.md). Test change: RT-1 fixture uploads the bytes before referencing them. Residual: peer-to-peer mode cannot prove possession, so identical content first referenced by another tenant is refused; a crafted manifest learned via the relay before the honest one can still adopt unowned P2P chunks if the attacker already knows the chunk hashes.

problems.title: Anonymous node-id hijack via shared kora:anonymous claim owner; forged high seq silently drops victim uploads

Provider user ids in the reserved kora: namespace are refused (AUTH_FAILED). Client half (W3 step 2, minimal): the engine never trusts the advertised own-node sequence above min(serverVector[self], last acknowledged own seq) for uploads and pending counts, and never persists the advertised own entry. Test change: RT-5 anonymous reconnect now presents the issued token. Migration: legacy kora:anonymous claims (only from pre-release builds of this branch) are not adopted; release them with releaseNodeClaim.

problems.title: Cross-tenant dangling child: uplink does not authorize foreign-key targets; owner can never delete parent
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: authorizeOperationReferences (server/src/scopes/reference-authorization.ts): for an insert, or an update that changes a relation field, the referenced parent must exist (soft-deleted counts, as stored) and be inside the writer DOWNLINK scope, else non-retriable SCOPE_VIOLATION naming only the writer record/field. Wired in ClientSession (after the validator, before apply) and scoped routes (prepareMutation and the store conditional path, reading inside the locked transaction). Only for authenticated scoped sessions (no tenant boundary otherwise). Test change: RT-10 seeds its cross-tenant children directly in the store (legacy data), since sync now refuses them. Residual: pre-check, not re-evaluated inside the apply critical section (a parent moved out of scope concurrently can still be referenced once).

problems.title: Ownership transfer discloses full pre-transfer edit history (historical ops judged on current row)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: every store captures an OperationScopeSnapshot {pre, post} (id + scalar fields, strings <= 512 chars) from its own rows inside the apply transaction (applyRemoteOperation, Postgres applyConditional) into operations.scope_snapshot (memory: map). Delivery stream (DeliveredOperation.scopeSnapshot), version-vector delta and live relay (getOperationScopeSnapshots) judge download scope on post; query subsets still use the current row. Migration: missing snapshots are backfilled from the log at setSchema (and after replace-mode backup import) by replaying each record in delivery order; ops without a snapshot (collections outside the schema, custom stores) fall back to the previous current-row rule. Behaviour change: a record that moves INTO a scope is delivered from the entering op only (no history; conflicts with the SRV-2 / W4 step 4 send-history design, which now needs a server-built snapshot instead); a previous owner resyncing receives the history written while it owned the record. LMS-11-pg benchmark assertion updated accordingly.

problems.title: Retraction injection via writer previousData (noise in other tenants' delivery logs)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: scope-exit retractions use snapshotExitsScopes on the store-captured pre/post values (pre = stored row before apply, a deleted row counts as absent); the writer previousData is never consulted. Ops without a snapshot never produce a retraction. Test change: client-session.test retract-mode test now inserts the record server-side first (its pre-image previously came from previousData).

problems.title: Directional uplink grants bypass resolveSessionScopes ($claims not resolved; fails closed)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: directional uplink grants go through resolveSessionScopes like the downlink (verified $claims bound to the schema, onUnresolved deny so a missing binding only removes write access, the handshake can only narrow, undefined/null values refused).

problems.title: Blob requests not rate-limited; cache invalidation triggers full scope rescans per write
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: blob-chunk-request charged to the session rate limiter (over budget answered "not held", no disconnect; counted in getIngestLimitCounts().rateLimitedBlobRequests). BlobAccessIndex shares one in-flight rebuild per scope and invalidates by collection generation (writes to collections without blob fields drop nothing; a rebuild invalidated mid-flight is not cached); the delivery poll invalidates only the collections written since the last poll (all beyond 1000 ops).

problems.title: Revocation listeners are in-process: other server instances keep revoked sessions until token expiry
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 2 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round2.md). Fixed: KoraSyncServer re-validates every live session credential with its auth provider every sessionRevalidationIntervalMs (default 30 s, 0 disables; also driven by the delivery poll tick) and on demand via revalidateSessions(); a refused credential or a different principal ends the session with retriable AUTH_REVOKED (AUTH_EXPIRED when past expiry); provider errors end nothing. Two-instance tests: shared in-memory user store, two SQLite handles on one file, two Postgres pools on one database (packages/auth/tests/repro/RT-18.test.ts). Not done: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY push (optional). Found while testing: PostgresUserStore cold-start DDL raced when two instances started at once (type already exists); fixed later: every auth Postgres store creates its tables in one transaction under an advisory lock, retrying an idempotent DDL that still loses a creation race (packages/auth/src/postgres/ensure-schema.ts).

problems.title: Record moving into scope never appears for the new owner (only the scope-changing update is delivered)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: when an operation moves an existing record into a session's download scope (store snapshot pre out, post in; scope fields a snapshot lacks judged on the current row), the server sends a synthesized scope-entry insert before the trigger on every path (delivery stream initial + live push, legacy version-vector delta, legacy relay). Built from the CURRENT materialized row (only while live and still in scope), id derived from (collection, recordId, trigger op id) (stable across paths and resends; delivery sequences are not available on the legacy paths), node 'kora:scope-entry', sequence 0, no deps, timestamp = record's newest HLC (new optional ServerStore.getRecordLatestTimestamp, memory/SQLite/Postgres) so it never overrides a newer client field. Delivery batches never end on an entry (entry and trigger share a delivery sequence). No pre-transfer history is sent (RT-14 tests unchanged). Client: inbound scope filter judged per op in apply order (a partial update in the same batch as its insert was dropped); an insert for a scope-retracted row reactivates it with per-field LWW. kora: node ids refused at handshake (INVALID_NODE_ID). The entry's single whole-row timestamp (createdAt = latest edit; a newer unsynced local edit of an older field overwritten, then diverging) is superseded by per-field versions: see RT-27.

problems.title: Schema migration adding/renaming a scope field: scope snapshots not recomputed, history hidden from fresh devices
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: stores fingerprint the scalar fields scope snapshots capture (memory field; kora_server_meta table in SQLite/Postgres) and, when it changes at setSchema, null every snapshot and rebuild them from the log (fingerprint written last; idempotent). Visibility, exits and entries judge a scope field ABSENT from a snapshot on the record's current row; a present value (including null, which over-long strings are now recorded as) still fails closed. Migration: the first start on this build recomputes every snapshot once (fingerprint absent).

problems.title: Anonymous device locked out permanently if node token is lost; legacy anonymous clients refused
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: anonymous claims are provisional (kora:anon-pending:<sha256(token)>:<expiresAt>) until the client acknowledges the handshake response with the saved token (AcknowledgmentMessage.nodeToken, protobuf field 39) or presents it at a later handshake (both confirm via CAS to kora:anon-node:<hash>). A provisional claim is re-issued to a token-less device when no live session (this instance) holds the node and it is younger than anonymousClaimTtlMs (default 24h). Expired provisional claims and legacy 'kora:anonymous' claims are re-issued only with allowLegacyAnonymousClaims (default true for beta.13, warns session.legacy_anonymous_claim). New optional store methods getNodeClaimOwner / replaceNodeClaim (memory/SQLite/Postgres). Client: NODE_ID_CLAIMED triggers Store.rotateNodeId (fresh UUIDv7 node, unsynced ops re-authored with seq 1..n, recomputed ids, remapped deps, re-stamped field versions, node token cleared, old node vector entry lowered), outbound queue replaced, event sync:node-id-rotated. Residual: an unconfirmed claim can be taken by any token-less anonymous device while its holder is disconnected (the holder then rotates; no data loss); liveness is per instance. A pinned StoreConfig.nodeId cannot rotate (NODE_ID_PINNED).

problems.title: FK target authorized against downlink only: children of uplink-only parents rejected (forms/surveys)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: authorizeOperationReferences accepts a foreign-key parent inside the writer's downlink OR uplink scope (ReferenceAuthorizationContext.uplinkScopes, passed by sync sessions). A parent in neither is still SCOPE_VIOLATION (RT-13 tests unchanged). Residual: with an uplink predicate wider than the downlink, existence of parent ids inside the uplink scope is observable via accept/refuse.

problems.title: Peer-relay mode (no central blob store): identical content in a second tenant permanently rejected
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: in peer-relay mode (no persistBlobChunk) the handshake response sets blobPossessionProof (protobuf field 40); the client upload coordinator pushes the bytes behind each reference; the session hash-verifies them, applies the size/quota and manifest checks, records the pusher in blob_owners and drops the bytes. Cross-tenant reads still refused (RT-1/RT-11 tests). Cost: each device uploads each blob once to the server even in P2P mode.

problems.title: Blob downloads share the op rate budget; "not held" treated as hard failure; large blobs fail
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: blob chunk requests use their own budget (blobLimits.maxRequestsPerMinute, default 6000/min) instead of maxOpsPerMinute; over budget the answer is a retriable {bytes:null, throttled:true, retryAfterMs} (protobuf fields 41-42), and createRemoteChunkProvider re-sends after max(minThrottleDelayMs, retryAfterMs) bounded by maxThrottleDelayMs until maxThrottleWaitMs (default 10 min).

problems.title: Content-hash existence oracle; pre-claimed hash lets claimer read bytes another tenant uploads later
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: with a central store (resolveBlobChunk) BlobAccessIndex.authorizeReference never claims an unowned hash; a reference is accepted only if the writer pushed the bytes or can already read a record referencing them. The store serves owners (BlobAccessIndex.isOwnedBy) or in-scope referencers. RT-11 guard test updated to push before referencing (the client's order since RT-11). Residual existence oracle (P2P bare-reference claims; non-constant timing) documented in docs/guide/production-server.md.

problems.title: Session revalidation checks identity only; scope/role changes apply at token expiry (document or compare scopes)
problems.notes: Phase 1 red-team round 3 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). Fixed: revalidateCredential re-resolves the session's scopes (computeSessionScopes, shared with the handshake, using the handshake's syncScope) and ends a session whose downlink or uplink scope changed, or no longer resolves, with retriable SCOPE_CHANGED. Documented in docs/guide/production-server.md.

problems.title: Scope-entry insert carries one whole-row timestamp: overwrites a device's newer unsynced edit of an older field, then client and server diverge (and createdAt = latest edit)
problems.notes: Follow-up to RT-19 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase1-round3.md). The synthesized scope-entry insert was stamped with the record's newest HLC for every field; under per-field LWW it beat a device's unsynced edit (t5) of a field the server last wrote earlier (t1) whenever any other field was newer (t7), after which the device's own op uploaded and won on the server: device and server diverged. Fixed: Operation gains optional fieldVersions (field -> HLC; server-authored only, not in the content hash). The server folds them from the record's stored operations exactly like the materialization (core replayFieldVersionsForRecord; new optional ServerStore.getRecordFieldVersions on memory/SQLite/Postgres, ordered in JS by HLC.compare); the entry carries them, and its timestamp is the record's first operation (server _created_at), so a fresh device's createdAt is the real creation time. Fields no op wrote get the creation version. Wire: JSON field + protobuf __kora_field_versions__ in the data JSON (static and dynamic serializers), validated on decode; the server strips fieldVersions from device-uploaded ops. Client: the apply pipeline routes an entry with fieldVersions straight to the store, which resolves each field by LWW against _field_versions (absent row: per-field stamps + orphan fold; live or scope-retracted row: per-field LWW; domain tombstone: revived only when the newest field version is newer), never a whole-row stamp; the clock receives the newest version; the client op log persists fieldVersions and record folds expand an entry into insert@creation + per-version updates (core expandFieldVersionedOperations). Stores without getRecordFieldVersions fall back to the RT-19 single stamp. Residual: richtext and atomic (counter) fields resolve by plain LWW in the entry path (a device's unsynced richtext/atomic edit older than the server's latest write to that field is overwritten locally while its op still merges on the server). Found while running the round-3 code on Postgres (none of it had run there): (1) the Postgres store ordered node-id ties by the database collation when folding a record (materialization, backfill, latest-timestamp), so under a linguistic collation (en_US/ICU: node-a < node-Z) the server row diverged from HLC.compare used by clients, memory and SQLite; now COLLATE "C" (postgres-round3.test.ts forces an ICU column collation); (2) LMS-11-pg counted RT-19 scope entries as unexplained extra ops; its reference now counts entries separately. The rt-fixture / scoped-network harnesses run on Postgres with KORA_REPRO_STORE=postgres.

problems.title: Ops made while offline stay counted as pending after the server has them (status accuracy)
problems.notes: Pending count is the queue plus the unscanned own tail, from the client's own acks (never min with the stale handshake vector); the engine notifies status bridges on ack/streaming so waitForSettled resolves promptly. Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-28.test.ts (both cases failed on the baseline engine).

problems.title: Scope entry: richtext and counter fields resolved by plain LWW; renamed fields lose versions; no MergeTrace
problems.notes: Residual of RT-27; resolved structurally by W7 per-field CRDT state. W7 Stage B1 (client): a scope-entry insert carrying Operation.foldState (server-authored serialized fold state, B3 wire / B2 server) is JOINED into the device's state (core mergeOp -> joinStates), so counters, custom resolvers, arrays and richtext keep the device's concurrent edits; one merge:conflict trace per field where the device and the server differed (strategy scope-entry-<strategy>). Entries from older servers (fieldVersions only) still merge per field. Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-29 (counter/resolver/array + traces) and packages/test/tests/fold-scope-entry-richtext.test.ts (real Yjs). End to end it needs the server to send foldState (B2/B3). 2 (server): Server half done: scope-entry ops carry foldState (serialized fold state filtered to the fields the entry restates; fieldVersions kept, now derived from the fold) built from ServerStore.getRecordFoldState; client-session passes it (2 call-site lines). Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-29.test.ts (memory + SQLite): joining the entry state with a receiver's concurrent counter/resolver/richtext writes equals the server fold of the union. Wire + client join are B3/B1.

problems.title: Live-Postgres parity tests fail under vitest with DATABASE_URL (dynamic import of postgres)
problems.acceptance: Write a repro when the workstream starts.
problems.notes: Found during RT-27 Postgres verification.

problems.title: Upgrade re-upload / renumbered own ops re-judged by today's authorization and validators: non-retriable rejection for ops the server already stores
problems.notes: Phase 2 seam (W3 upgrade re-upload x server ingest). handleOperationBatch authorized, timestamp/size-checked and ran validateOperation before learning the op was stored; isStoredOperation looked up by (node, seq) only, so an op renumbered by the client sequence repair (same id, new seq) was not recognised either. Fixed: optional ServerStore.findStoredOperations(ids) -> Map<id,{nodeId,sequenceNumber}> (memory, SQLite, Postgres; one chunked IN read per batch, after the first rate-limit charge). An own-node op whose id is stored under this node is acked as a duplicate before any other check (any sequence). Foreign ops keep NODE_ID_MISMATCH unless the exact (node, seq, id) is stored (echo). Stores without the method fall back to a per-op (node, seq) lookup. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-31.test.ts; unit tests in packages/server/src/session/session-hardening.test.ts.

problems.title: Legacy duplicate (node, seq) from beta.12: the op the client repair keeps is refused SEQUENCE_CONFLICT when the server holds the other half
problems.notes: Phase 2 seam (W6 sequence repair x SRV-4 SEQUENCE_CONFLICT). Fixed with a server sequence-enforcement epoch: on the first start of this release each SQL store records MAX(delivery_seq) in kora_server_meta.sequence_enforcement_epoch (memory store: 0). SEQUENCE_CONFLICT is raised only when a holder of the (node, seq) was stored after the epoch; a legacy-only holder is accepted and stored with a console warning (as beta.12 did). The conditional full unique index is replaced by a partial unique index idx_node_seq_unique_after_epoch ON operations(node_id, sequence_number) WHERE delivery_seq > epoch, which always exists. Replace-mode backup import moves the epoch to the restored log's end. Postgres insertOperationRow now checks every holder (re-applying one op of a legacy pair was a false conflict with LIMIT 1). Store tests: packages/server/src/store/sequence-enforcement-epoch.test.ts (SQLite, Postgres via KORA_PG_TEST_URL, memory). E2E repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-32.test.ts.

problems.title: SYNC-11 server half: an auth-scoped client's reconnect restarts the delivery stream from 0 (full rescan and resend every reconnect)
problems.notes: The client reports the watermark of its REQUESTED scope; when the server resolves a different scope it could not trust it and restarted at 0 on every reconnect. Fixed: the client persists the downlink scope the server last accepted (SyncStatePersistence load/saveAcceptedDownlinkScope, restored) and its handshake additionally sends acceptedScopeKey (scopeViewKey: canonical JSON of the normalized scope map, packages/sync/src/scopes/scope-view-key.ts, shared by client and server) and acceptedScopeWatermark (that view's own watermark). New optional protocol fields, JSON and protobuf 43/44. The server computes scopeViewKey of the scope it resolves now and resumes from acceptedScopeWatermark when the keys match, else starts the view from 0 (a widened grant delivers the newly visible records). The accepted scope is never sent as the requested scope. A grant equal (by key) to the request keeps the requested view on the client. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-33.test.ts (resume counts sent ops and scan cursors; widened grant). The handshake node pre-scan for scoped clients stays (beta.13 clients count pending from the handshake vector; kora compact uses peer entries); it now starts at the resumed watermark.

problems.title: Node rotation lowers or deletes the old node's version-vector entry and writes the vector outside the W6 discipline (scan before the transaction, INSERT OR REPLACE)
problems.acceptanceTest: packages/store/src/sync/rotate-node-id.test.ts (3 tests failed before the fix: old entry lowered to the highest remaining op, deleted when every op rotated, and a counter advanced by another writer after the pre-transaction scan overwritten)
problems.notes: Phase 2 seam (W6 x RT-21). rotateUnsyncedOperationsInLog scanned the old node's ops before its transaction and wrote _kora_version_vector with INSERT OR REPLACE: the old node's counter dropped to its highest remaining op (or was deleted), so a rotated op that reached the server unacknowledged could have its number reused by a writer still on the old id (another tab): SEQUENCE_CONFLICT on the server. Fixed: the scan, rewrite and vector writes run in one transaction; the new node's entry is an UPSERT with MAX(stored, new); the old node's entry is never lowered (rotated numbers become holes, which upload tracking resolves). Store.rotateNodeId takes its counter from the persisted vector. A grep found no other vector write outside the discipline except backup restore (STORE-5, Phase 3, untouched).

problems.title: Op uploaded and acked before it is durable locally (IndexedDB 500 ms snapshot debounce): after losing the tail the next write reuses the sequence (non-retriable SEQUENCE_CONFLICT, never synced) and the lost op is never re-delivered to its author (permanent divergence)
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Locations: store/src/adapters/indexeddb-adapter.ts:95 (debounced snapshot; flushPersistence has no caller in sync); sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:1541 (only a LOWER advertised own entry is acted on; the local counter is never raised to the server's); server/src/session/client-session.ts:2010, 2649-2657 (own ops excluded from a resumed stream); server/src/apply/apply-server-operation.ts:256 (SEQUENCE_CONFLICT terminal). Same outcome after restoring an older local copy (OS/Electron backup). Required fix: flush the IndexedDB snapshot before an op is marked sent; at handshake raise the local counter above an advertised own entry (MAX, in a transaction) and have the server re-send own ops above the client's own vector entry regardless of watermark; treat SEQUENCE_CONFLICT against the device's own lost op as recoverable (fetch the holder, renumber the new write). Repro simulates the lost tail by restoring a VACUUM INTO snapshot. FIXED (client, branch worktree-agent-ac713ddaf488cccee): upload batches are flagged sent (persisted) and the store durability barrier (StorageAdapter.ensureDurable; IndexedDB generation-tracked snapshot barrier) is awaited before the wire; handshake raises the persisted counter past an advertised own entry (in-tx MAX), resets delivery to a full resync (own ops included) and reconnects; SEQUENCE_CONFLICT on an own upload renumbers it (same id) above the server entry and resyncs. Client advertises handshake sequenceReservation: true. Server-side targeted resend of own ops above the client vector not done (client full resync instead).

problems.title: Own-log rescan (upgrade re-upload, server-advertised lower prefix) resubmits ops the server terminally rejected: a refused write is re-judged and applied later
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:2807-2840 scanOwnLog enqueues every own op not queued and inside the uplink scope, never consulting the rejected store; the prefix restarts at 0 on upgrade (2680) or is lowered by lowerOwnPrefixLocked. Repro: a withdrawal refused (INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, non-retriable) is applied after the upgrade re-upload once the balance allows it. Required fix: persist terminal rejections as resolved per op id in a durable marker the app cannot clear, and skip them in scanOwnLog and rotation; optionally the server remembers refused ids and answers a resubmission with the original rejection. Fix RT-37 first (beta.13 SEQUENCE_CONFLICT losses are currently only rescued by this bug). FIXED (client): durable _kora_terminal_rejections markers (app cannot clear), written before the prefix passes the op; scanOwnLog and RT-21 re-authoring skip them; seeded once from _kora_sync_rejected excluding SEQUENCE_CONFLICT/NODE_ID_MISMATCH/OUT_OF_UPLINK_SCOPE so beta.13 SEQUENCE_CONFLICT writes still re-upload (and are renumbered if refused again).

problems.title: Mixed versions: beta.13 clients still create duplicate (node, seq) pairs (concurrent app.transaction); the Phase 2 server refuses the second op with non-retriable SEQUENCE_CONFLICT for every pair created after the server upgrade, and the beta.13 engine drops the write
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Verified end to end with the real beta.13 build (33bca46, scratch harness): two concurrent app.transaction inserts share seq 1; synced to this branch's server, the second is recorded rejected SEQUENCE_CONFLICT and never stored. Location: server/src/store/server-store.ts:63-76 judgeSequenceHolders (conflict when any holder is after the epoch); server/src/apply/apply-server-operation.ts:252-258. Also on Postgres (KORA_REPRO_STORE=postgres); during a rolling upgrade a beta.13 instance's insert of such a pair hits idx_node_seq_unique_after_epoch. Required fix: enforce SEQUENCE_CONFLICT only for clients that advertise the W6 sequence guarantee (new handshake capability); for older clients store the pair as a legacy pair with a warning (beta.13 server behaviour) or answer retriably; document upgrade order. Repro drives the beta.13 upload at protocol level. Fixed (server + protocol): new optional handshake capability HandshakeMessage.sequenceReservation?: boolean (JSON; protobuf envelope field 45, bool), set by clients that reserve sequence numbers in-transaction. ClientSession reads it at handshake; a session without it is a legacy sequence client (isLegacySequenceClient()) and applies with ApplyRemoteOptions.legacySequenceWriter: judgeSequenceHolders then never refuses a held sequence for that writer: the second op is stored as a legacy pair (own delivery sequence, so the delivery stream, live relay and getOperationRange version-vector path deliver both), with a console warning, a structured log event session.legacy_sequence_pair and onLegacySequencePair/getLegacySequencePairCount(). Capable clients and server-originated ops still get SEQUENCE_CONFLICT. Index redesign (SQLite + Postgres): new column operations.seq_unique INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, set to 1 only when the row was the sole holder of its (node, seq) at insert; the partial unique index is now idx_node_seq_unique_sole ON operations(node_id, sequence_number) WHERE seq_unique = 1 (idx_node_seq_unique and idx_node_seq_unique_after_epoch are dropped at startup; flagged duplicates from outside writes are unflagged before the index is recreated). A legacy pair is never in the index, and an older instance's insert during a rolling upgrade (column default 0) never hits it; two concurrent sole inserts still collide. Replace-mode backup rows are inserted unflagged. Memory store keeps every holder per (node, seq). Upgrade order: servers first, then clients; a client is only held to SEQUENCE_CONFLICT once it advertises the capability. Tests: packages/sync/src/protocol/sequence-reservation-wire.test.ts; packages/server/src/store/sequence-enforcement-epoch.test.ts (legacy writer contract on memory, SQLite, Postgres); packages/server/tests/integration/legacy-sequence-and-ingest-budget.test.ts (session level, memory/SQLite/Postgres).

problems.title: Node rotation (RT-21) uploads the previous user's unsynced writes on the next user's session when users share one local database (no namespaceByAuthUser): authorized, validated and attributed as the new user; sent-but-unacked ops are stored twice
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:1582-1640 rotateNodeIdentity re-queues every own op above the prefix regardless of who wrote it; NODE_ID_CLAIMED is exactly what a second user on the same database receives. Repro: Alice's offline note is submitted with ctx.auth.userId = bob. A rotated op that was sent but not acknowledged keeps its old copy on the server and gains a re-authored copy (atomic increments double). Required fix: bind unsynced ops to the principal that wrote them; on NODE_ID_CLAIMED for a different principal hold the other user's ops (surface them; upload when that user signs in) or require namespaceByAuthUser with auth; never rotate ops flagged sent. FIXED (client): uploads bound to the session node; on NODE_ID_CLAIMED for a previously accepted node its unsynced writes are held (status.heldOperations) and the device switches to a held node untried in this refusal cycle or a fresh one; never-accepted nodes keep RT-21 re-authoring minus ops flagged sent (the double-store cause). namespaceByAuthUser default unchanged (see report).

problems.title: Upgrade re-upload charged op by op to the ingest rate limit (600/min) although every op is a stored duplicate: RATE_LIMIT ends the session every minute and new writes wait behind the whole history
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Location: server/src/session/client-session.ts:2236-2251 (rate limiter charged before the stored-id lookup); RATE_LIMIT is a session error (engine disconnects and backs off, downloads interrupted); the outbound queue is HLC-ordered so new writes follow the old history. Repro: 1,500-op history, server restarted with default limits, a fresh write is not on the server after 5 reconnects and RATE_LIMIT was sent. Required fix: look up stored ids first (batch already capped) and do not charge stored duplicates (or use a separate larger budget); make RATE_LIMIT a per-batch retriable throttle with retryAfterMs instead of a session error; upload new writes ahead of the re-upload backlog. Fixed (server): handleOperationBatch charges one rate-limit unit per batch for the stored-id lookup (BATCH_LOOKUP_RATE_COST, credited against the first charged op, so N new ops still cost N), then acks operations the lookup finds stored (own op under this node, or exact (node, seq, id) echo) as duplicates with no per-op charge. Every other op is charged before any store work as before (RT-6). The ingest limiter is keyed per device node (KoraSyncServer.rateLimiterFor), so one node's re-upload never throttles another node of the same user (test added). RATE_LIMIT text now includes the retry delay. Not done here (client engine / ErrorMessage, other owners): RATE_LIMIT is still a connection-level error message (retriable: true) rather than a per-batch throttle with a retryAfterMs field, and new writes are not reordered ahead of a re-upload backlog. Tests: packages/server/tests/integration/legacy-sequence-and-ingest-budget.test.ts; repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-39.test.ts green. Follow-up (Phase 2 round 2, not attacked by the red team): the per-node limiter could be multiplied by minting node ids, so KoraSyncServer now layers a per-principal budget (maxOpsPerMinutePerUser, default 4 x maxOpsPerMinute, 0 disables; user map with the same TTL/LRU bounds as the node map) on the per-node one via CombinedRateLimiter: a refusal by the user budget spends none of the node budget, and a node over its own budget spends none of the user budget, so per-node fairness and the per-batch lookup cost are unchanged. Anonymous and NoAuth sessions have no stable principal and keep only the per-node budget. Tests: session-operation-limits.test.ts, operation-resolutions.test.ts (per-user ingest budget).

problems.title: per-tab isolation: a closed tab's unsynced writes (own node id, shared database) are never uploaded by later tabs and never counted pending
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:2680-2700 and 2761-2800 (own tracking bound to store.getNodeId()); store/src/store/tab-node-id.ts (sessionStorage node per tab). Required fix: persist the set of node ids this database authored with a prefix per node; a starting engine adopts orphaned per-tab nodes under a Web Lock and uploads their unacknowledged ops (server side: node-claim handover for those nodes under auth). FIXED (client): local node registry + per-tab Web Lock; a starting engine adopts a local node with unsynced writes and a free lock, runs a session as that node (original ids), then reconnects; other local nodes count as pending.

problems.title: app.storage.deleteDatabase() unsynced check counts only _kora_sync_queue rows; own ops above own_acked_through that are not queued (upgrade re-upload pending, op committed before an un-awaited pushOperation persisted, closed per-tab tab) are deleted
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md). Location: kora/src/storage-accessor.ts:15-36 hasUnsyncedOperations. Required fix: unsynced = queue rows OR any own op (any local node id) above its own_acked_through OR a node with no recorded prefix; keep the local-only branch. FIXED: deleteDatabase unsynced check = queue OR any local node own op above its prefix (no prefix: from 0) minus terminal rejections (store/internal hasUnsyncedOwnOperations).

problems.title: Unsynced writes are bound to a node, not to the principal that wrote them: a write made after a user switch but before the next accepted handshake is held for the previous user and later uploaded as that user; a never-accepted node's writes are uploaded as whoever handshakes first
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Residual of RT-38. Locations: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:1717 holdNodeAndSwitch (holds EVERY unsynced op of the refused node, including the new user's own writes authored under it before the refusal), 1759 reauthorUnsentAndRotate and 1536 recordNodeAccepted (a node's owner is learned only at the first accepted handshake), 3200 chooseSessionNode (adopts a never-accepted per-tab node under the current principal). Repro 1: Alice synced on NA; Bob signs in and writes before his first handshake; NA is refused and held: Bob's write is held while he is signed in (heldOperations>0) and is submitted with ctx.auth.userId = alice when Alice signs back in. Repro 2: a database that never synced: Alice's offline writes are uploaded on Bob's session. Required fix: bind each write to the principal known locally at write time (the auth layer knows who is signed in): rotate or switch the node id when the signed-in principal changes, BEFORE the next write (not on NODE_ID_CLAIMED), record the principal per local node, and never upload a node's writes on another principal's session; or make namespaceByAuthUser the default when auth is configured. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-42.test.ts. FIXED (client, auth-aware apps): local writes are bound to the signed-in user. Store.bindPrincipal(user) (new _kora_local_nodes.principal column, added in place by ALTER TABLE on open) moves the store to that user's own node, or a fresh one, BEFORE the next write; createApp calls it at start and on every auth change of sync.authClient (AuthSyncCoordinator -> SyncEngine.refreshPrincipal(), which ends the previous user's session first). The engine (SyncConfig.principal) never uploads, adopts or rotates into a node bound to another user: its writes are reported in status.heldOperations and upload as their owner when they sign in again. Pinned node ids (auth dev claim) cannot move: another user suspends sync (reason node-owned-by-another-user). per-tab: the tab moves to a fresh per-tab node. The repro now models an auth-aware device (TestDevice principal + authChanged()); a client never told who is signed in cannot tell users apart (documented residual, docs/guide/authentication.md). namespaceByAuthUser default unchanged (false): switching it on would hide the shared database's data without a migration; principal binding gives per-user node isolation without it. Writes issued before the auth binding reports a sign-in (same tick) are still authored under the previous user's node and held for them (documented; AuthBoundKoraProvider avoids it). Tests: packages/store/src/store/principal-binding.test.ts, sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-42 block), kora auth-sync-coordinator.test.ts + create-app.test.ts, packages/test/tests/phase2-node-fairness.test.ts.

problems.title: An acknowledged own op the server does not store under its sequence (validator action ignore; W6-renumbered op stored under its old number) at the tail makes every handshake look like a restored server: the tail is re-uploaded and re-validated on every reconnect
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:1634 (advertisedOwn < ownAckedThrough lowers the prefix on every handshake); the server's handshake vector is MAX(stored sequence) per node (server/src/session/client-session.ts:1942-1986), and client-session.ts:2425-2429 acknowledges an ignored op without storing anything. Repro: the newest own op is ignored by validateOperation (out-of-band handling, e.g. send an invoice): after 5 reconnects the validator has seen it 6 times; its out-of-band effect repeats. Same shape for a W6 sequence-repaired op whose stored copy keeps the old number (free duplicate re-upload each reconnect). Ends only when the device writes something newer. Required fix: the server must advertise per node the highest sequence it has RESOLVED (stored, ignored, or terminally refused), e.g. a per-node acknowledged-through column, not MAX(stored); or the client must confirm a lower advertisement by id (ask which of its ops above X the server holds) before lowering the prefix, and lower it at most once per server incarnation. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-43.test.ts. Fixed (server): the handshake's own-node entry is max(stored max, highest RESOLVED sequence) for the node. ClientSession durably records (awaited before the answer) an op the validator ignored ('ignored'), a terminal non-retriable refusal ('refused', excluding SEQUENCE_CONFLICT, which the client renumbers and resubmits under the same id), and an own op acked as a duplicate of a copy stored under another sequence ('stored-elsewhere'); retriable rejections are never resolutions. A resubmitted ignored/stored-elsewhere id is acknowledged as a duplicate without re-running the validator. Store schema: new tables operation_resolutions(op_id PK, node_id, sequence_number, outcome ignored|refused|stored-elsewhere, code, message, resolved_at; index (node_id, sequence_number)) and sequence_pairs(node_id, sequence_number PK) on SQLite and Postgres (created at startup, IF NOT EXISTS; pairs backfilled once from the log, flag sequence_pairs_backfilled in kora_server_meta); memory store keeps both in maps. A replace-mode importBackup rebuilds sequence_pairs and drops resolutions above each node's restored log (they would hide stored ops the restore lost). Tests: packages/server/tests/integration/operation-resolutions.test.ts (memory, SQLite, Postgres); repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-43.test.ts green.

problems.title: Cloned database (one node id on two live devices) is never detected: each copy's writes are own operations for the other (never delivered on a resumed stream or live relay), and every sequence collision costs a renumber plus a full resync from 0
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Locations: server/src/session/client-session.ts:2703-2711 (own-node ops skipped above ownOperationsIncludedThrough), sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:3383 recoverSequenceConflict (renumber + resetDeliveryForFullResync per collision), 1609-1625 (handshake raise + full resync). Repro: copy of a synced database opened as a second device; 3 writes on each while both are connected: the original never sees 2 of the copy's writes until a reconnect; 4 history-behind recoveries (each a full resync) for 6 writes. Converges after reconnects with no loss (verified). Required fix: detect a clone (the server sees two live sessions of one node, or a SEQUENCE_CONFLICT whose holder is not in the device's log yet was uploaded after the device's last handshake) and move one copy to a fresh node id (RT-21 re-authoring of its unsynced ops); at minimum rate-limit full resyncs. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-44.test.ts. FIXED (client): a SEQUENCE_CONFLICT for an own write whose sequence is above the session's handshake own entry means the holder was stored during this session by another live copy of the database: the copy moves to a fresh node id (rotateUnsent: the refused write, certainly not stored, and every never-sent one are re-authored; sent-unacked ones stay under the old node), ends the session and resyncs from 0 (sync:local-node clone-detected, no history-behind). The old node is forgotten when nothing of this copy waits under it. Fallback for stores that cannot rotate (pinned ids): recovery full resyncs are rate-limited to one per 60 s per engine (deferred to the next session start). A clone that collides only at or below the handshake entry (both copies wrote while offline) is first handled as RT-35 (renumber + resync) and detected at its next live collision. Tests: sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-44 blocks).

problems.title: Server restored from an older backup: a device whose node has no operation in the backup never re-uploads the operations the server lost (absent own vector entry read as "no information"); they exist only on devices
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Location: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:1634 `advertisedOwn !== undefined && advertisedOwn < this.ownAckedThrough`: the handshake vector omits a node the server holds nothing of (client-session.ts:1975-1977 filters serverVector), so advertisedOwn is undefined and the prefix is never lowered. Repro: devices a and b; backup taken when only a had written; then 3 increments each; server restored: a re-uploads its 3 (once), b never does: server count 6 instead of 66, serverOps 4 instead of 7; both devices show 66 and pendingOperations 0 (deleteDatabase would call b synced). New devices never receive b's writes. Required fix: the server always includes the session's own node in the handshake vector (0 when absent), and the client treats an absent own entry as 0 (lowering to 0 is safe: the server dedups by id). Combine with the RT-43 fix (resolved-through, not MAX(stored)). Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-45.test.ts. Fixed (server half): the handshake response always carries the session's own node, 0 when the server holds nothing of it (and the resolved-through value of RT-43 otherwise); only the own node is added, so RT-7 holds. The repro passes with the server half alone: the engine already lowers its prefix for any advertised own entry below its acknowledged prefix, and 0 is now advertised. The client half (an ABSENT own entry read as 0, for servers that omit it, e.g. beta.13) is owned by the client-engine fix and is defence in depth. Tests: operation-resolutions.test.ts (own node always advertised, RT-7 not echoed; replace import prunes resolutions past the restored log); client-session.test.ts handshake expectation updated; repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-45.test.ts green. IXED (client half; repro green with the client alone): the engine reads an ABSENT own entry in the handshake vector as 0 (the server names the session's node whenever it holds an op of it), lowers the acknowledged prefix and re-uploads (sync:local-node server-behind); the server dedups by id. The server half (always include the session's node, 0 when absent) is owned by the server workstream and is complementary. Until RT-43's server fix lands, a node whose ops the server only ignored (never stored) is absent and gets re-uploaded at each handshake (RT-43 class). Tests: sync own-node-bound.test.ts (own=0, absent, fresh device); no-silent-loss.test.ts upgrade-recovery mock now advertises what it stores.

problems.title: Per-tab adoption (RT-40) is head-of-line blocking: a session adopts one orphaned node and uploads nothing else until all its writes are acknowledged; one retriably rejected adopted write stalls the live tab's own uploads and every other orphan node, forever (cross-node parent/child deadlock)
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Locations: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:3200 chooseSessionNode (adopts the first eligible node in registry order on every start), 3175 isSessionOperation / takeBatch (only the session node uploads), 3422 maybeEndSessionForNodeWork (adoption ends only when the adopted prefix reaches its counter). Repro: two closed per-tab tabs, the OLDER node holds a task whose parent project is on the NEWER node; the app validator defers a child until its parent is on the server (retriable: true). The remaining tab adopts the older node forever: after 6 reconnects NOTHING is on the server (not the parent, not the child, not the open tab's own write). Control without the deferral: all three sync. Same stall with any persistent retriable rejection (throwing validator, RATE_LIMIT) of an adopted write. Required fix: upload the live tab's own writes and other nodes' writes alongside an adoption (one session per node, or multiplex by bounded time slices), give up an adoption that makes no progress and move on round-robin, and order adoption by causal dependencies across local nodes (a cross-node causalDep must upload first). Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-46.test.ts. FIXED (client): local nodes take turns, one session each (the server confines uploads to the session node). chooseSessionNode skips a parked adoption (its last session ended with a batch the server did not process, e.g. a retriable deferral) until the database's upload-progress counter moved or its backoff (30 s doubling, max 1 h) ran out, orders adoptions by cross-node causal deps (a node whose unsynced ops name another local node's unsynced op goes after it; cycles broken in registry order), and an adopted node that stalls is parked and its session ended at once (sync:local-node adoption-parked). The own node's session yields once its own uploads made progress and a deferred node became worth retrying (causal parent uploaded, or parked >= 30 s and progress moved). Schedule persisted in _kora_meta sync_adoption_schedule_v1 (SyncStatePersistence.load/saveAdoptionSchedule, in memory otherwise). Residual: a session-level error (not a per-op rejection) recurring on an adopted node's batch is not parked. Tests: sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-46 block), packages/test/tests/phase2-node-fairness.test.ts (3 closed tabs + open tab, one write deferred forever).

problems.title: RT-36 residual: the terminal-rejection marker is client-only and not covered by any durability barrier; a device that loses the tail of its database after a rejection (IndexedDB 500 ms window, restored copy) resubmits the refused op, and the server applies it
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Locations: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:2780-2785 (recordTerminalRejections on a non-retriable rejection; no durability barrier before the outcome is acted on), store/src/sync/local-sync-records.ts:111; server keeps no record of refused ids (server/src/session/client-session.ts sendOperationRejected). Repro: the device database is snapshotted while the server judges the upload (sent flag durable, rejection not yet received), the refusal (INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS) is recorded, the snapshot is restored, the balance recovers: the withdrawal is applied. Required fix: the server remembers refused operation ids (with the original code) and answers a resubmission with the original rejection (the optional half of the RT-36 fix); client side, flush the marker durably (ensureDurable) before acting on the rejection. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-47.test.ts. Fixed (server): a terminal refusal is recorded (code, message) in operation_resolutions before the rejection is sent; a later upload of the same id under the session's own node is answered from the table with the original rejection (retriable false) before authorization, validators or any store work, and charged nothing beyond the batch lookup unit. Lookups are keyed by the session's own (claimed) node id, so another device or tenant reusing the id is judged normally and learns nothing (not an oracle). Not done here (client engine, other owner): flushing the client-side marker durably before acting on the rejection. Store schema: new tables operation_resolutions(op_id PK, node_id, sequence_number, outcome ignored|refused|stored-elsewhere, code, message, resolved_at; index (node_id, sequence_number)) and sequence_pairs(node_id, sequence_number PK) on SQLite and Postgres (created at startup, IF NOT EXISTS; pairs backfilled once from the log, flag sequence_pairs_backfilled in kora_server_meta); memory store keeps both in maps. A replace-mode importBackup rebuilds sequence_pairs and drops resolutions above each node's restored log (they would hide stored ops the restore lost). Tests: operation-resolutions.test.ts (original rejection replayed, validator not re-run; cross-node id reuse judged normally; retriable and SEQUENCE_CONFLICT not remembered); repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-47.test.ts green.

problems.title: The second op of an RT-37 legacy pair never reaches a version-vector client that already holds the first (getOperationRange starts above the client's entry); mixed fleets diverge on vector clients
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Location: server/src/session/client-session.ts:2517 collectDeltaOperations (range clientSeq + 1 .. serverSeq per node). Repro (memory, SQLite and Postgres 16): a beta.13 writer uploads X@1; a vector client receives it and disconnects; the writer's concurrent transaction Y@1 is stored as a legacy pair; the vector client reconnects with {writer: 1} and receives nothing. The live relay covers only a connected peer; the delivery stream (watermark clients) is fine. The beta.13 server had the same gap; RT-37 keeps creating such pairs for every beta.13 writer. Required fix: the vector delta also sends ops stored as the non-sole holder of a (node, seq) at or below the client's entry that were stored after the client's last session (track per-node pair delivery sequences), or force vector clients to a full resync when the server stored a legacy pair for a node they track; document that vector clients must upgrade. Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-48.test.ts. Fixed (server): stores index legacy pairs in sequence_pairs at append (verdict 'legacy') and by a one-time backfill of the existing log; collectDeltaOperations sends, for every node a version-vector client reports, the members of each pair at or below min(client entry, server entry) ahead of the range above the entry. The client dedups by id; pairs come only from legacy writers, so the resend per handshake is small (it repeats at every handshake of a vector client: such clients should upgrade). New store method ServerStore.getSequencePairOperations (optional). Pairs written by an older server instance sharing the database during a rolling upgrade are not indexed until the next replace import. Tests: operation-resolutions.test.ts (pair index at append and after import; session delivery); repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-48.test.ts green on memory, SQLite and Postgres 16.

problems.title: A permanent local persistence failure (IndexedDB quota exceeded) makes the RT-35 durability barrier stop every upload while the app keeps writing in memory: writes the reachable server could have kept are lost on reload
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 2, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 2). Locations: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:2074-2093 sendUpload (barrier failure returns the batch and retries forever, UPLOAD_NOT_DURABLE), 1926-1932 (initial delta); store/src/adapters/indexeddb-persistence-scheduler.ts flushBarrier. Repro: the store's ensureDurable rejects (QuotaExceededError) after the first sync; a new write never reaches the reachable server after 3 reconnects. Since RT-35, a device that loses its tail recovers it from the server (handshake raise + full resync, renumber on SEQUENCE_CONFLICT), so uploading a non-durable op is no longer what loses data; withholding it is. Required fix: treat a persistently failing barrier (N attempts or T seconds, or a quota error) as degraded mode: upload anyway (the RT-35 recovery covers the reuse), surface a sync status error (store not durable) so the app can warn the user, and keep the barrier for transient failures. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-49.test.ts. FIXED (client): the durability barrier before an upload is bounded: after 3 consecutive failures the engine uploads anyway (degraded mode: status.localDurability = 'degraded', sync:durability-degraded and store:persistence-error DURABILITY_DEGRADED once); transient failures still postpone (UPLOAD_NOT_DURABLE). The barrier is still attempted before every upload and its first success restores (sync:durability-restored). RT-35 recovery restores a lost tail after reload. Tests: sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-49 tests).

problems.title: Store.bindPrincipal binds an UNBOUND node to the first user who signs in, without asking who owns it: on every database created before the RT-42 fix, the first sign-in after the upgrade adopts another user's node (their unsynced writes stranded forever, or uploaded as the wrong user)
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 3, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 3). Locations: store/src/store/store.ts:1547 (bindPrincipal: owner === null -> setLocalNodePrincipal(current node, principal)); kora/src/initialize-app.ts:152 (bind at start); sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:1868 holdNodeAndSwitch (NODE_ID_CLAIMED never corrects the local binding of the refused node). All pre-fix nodes have principal NULL. (1) Shared device, Bob left unsynced writes on his node NB, Alice signs in first after the upgrade: NB is bound to Alice locally, the server refuses it for Alice (claimed by Bob) so it is held; when Bob signs in NB belongs to another principal locally, so it is never uploaded or adopted: stranded forever (heldOperations 1). (2) A pre-upgrade database that never synced (Alice wrote offline): the first user to sign in after the upgrade (Bob) gets Alice's node and her writes are uploaded as Bob, so the RT-42 never-synced case is still open for existing databases. Required fix: never bind an unbound node that has unsynced writes by inference; learn its owner from the server (bind at the first ACCEPTED handshake as the session principal; on NODE_ID_CLAIMED clear an inferred binding instead of keeping it), and hold an unbound never-synced node with writes for an explicit app decision (surface it) instead of giving it to the first user. Record whether a binding is inferred or confirmed. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-50.test.ts (two tests). FIXED (store, sync, kora): Store.bindPrincipal never guesses the owner of an unbound node. An unbound node with no history (no write, never accepted) is bound in place (binding 'fresh'); one with history keeps no owner and the store moves to the user's own node (or a fresh one); a pinned unbound node stays in use unbound until the server decides. _kora_local_nodes gains binding ('fresh' | 'server' | 'app') and refused_principals. The engine learns owners from the server: an unbound node accepted before is adopted once per signed-in user; an accepted handshake binds it (confirmLocalNodePrincipal, 'server'); NODE_ID_CLAIMED records the user as refused for it and clears a guessed ('app' or legacy) binding, without holding it for good (markLocalNodeRefused held=false for unbound nodes). A never-synced unbound node with writes is held as 'unassigned' (status.heldNodes, heldOperations) until the app calls app.sync.assignHeld(nodeId, 'current-user') or app.sync.discardHeld(nodeId) (writes stay local, terminal marker HELD_DISCARDED). Rotation carries the binding to the re-authored node. Tests: store principal-binding.test.ts (RT-50 tests), sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-50), packages/test/tests/phase2-held-writes.test.ts, kora sync-control.test.ts. Documented in docs/guide/authentication.md, sync-configuration.md, api/sync.md.

problems.title: A 'stored-elsewhere' resolution acknowledges an upload the server does not store: after a replace-mode backup import the record outlives its stored copy and every re-upload of that id is acked and dropped
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 3, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 3). Locations: server/src/session/client-session.ts:2324 (any resolution hit for an id the batch lookup did NOT find stored is acked as a duplicate; for 'stored-elsewhere' that claim was just disproved by the lookup); server/src/store/{memory-server-store.ts:37, sqlite-server-store.ts:62, postgres-server-store.ts:73} (replace import prunes only resolutions ABOVE the restored node max, whatever their outcome). Sequence: ops 1..11 stored, backup; X stored at 12 (W6 renumber); a stale copy of X re-submitted at 5 (restored device copy) -> 'stored-elsewhere' at 5; replace import of the backup (X gone, resolution at 5 <= 11 kept); the device re-uploads X -> acked, never stored, no replica receives it. Fails on memory, SQLite and Postgres 16. Narrow (needs a renumber, a stale resubmission and a restore), but it is a silent ack-without-store. Required fix: treat a 'stored-elsewhere' hit for an id the lookup did not find as stale (judge the op normally, and delete the record); on replace import drop every 'stored-elsewhere' resolution whose id is not in the restored log. Also consider exporting resolutions in backups (today a migrated server forgets every refusal, RT-47 protection lost). Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-51.test.ts. FIXED (server): a stored-elsewhere resolution hit for an id the batch lookup did not find stored is stale: the session deletes it (new optional ServerStore.deleteOperationResolution, memory/SQLite/Postgres) and judges the op normally, recording its real outcome. Replace-mode import also drops stored-elsewhere resolutions whose op id is not in the restored log. Tests: server tests/integration/operation-resolutions.test.ts (RT-51 store and session tests, memory/SQLite/Postgres 16). Residual: backups still do not carry operation_resolutions (a migrated server forgets refusals, RT-47).

problems.title: RT-42 residual is much wider than 'the same instant': AuthSyncCoordinator queues a user switch behind any in-flight auth reconnect (credential fetch + up to 10 s connect), and every write the new user makes meanwhile is authored under the previous user's node and uploaded as that user
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 3, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 3). Cross-principal. Locations: kora/src/auth-sync-coordinator.ts:66 scheduleReconnect (a change during a run only sets pending), :90 run (refreshPrincipal, then engine.reconnect() which awaits stop/start); sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:639 (start binds the principal BEFORE the credential fetch and transport.connect at :714, so a session can also hand-shake a node bound to the previous user with the next user's token). Repro: Alice's token refresh starts a reconnect on a slow network; Bob signs in (binding reports it) and writes; the write is authored under Alice's node and later submitted as Alice. docs/guide/authentication.md says only writes 'in the same instant as a sign-in' are affected. Required fix: apply the principal binding synchronously on every auth event, outside the serialized reconnect (bind the store first, then queue the reconnect), and re-check the principal against the session node's owner after the credential fetch, before the handshake. At least document the real window. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-52.test.ts. FIXED (sync, kora): AuthSyncCoordinator.scheduleReconnect binds the store at once on every auth event via SyncEngine.bindSignedInUser(), outside the serialized reconnect (a live session keeps running as the previous user's node and uploads only that node's writes). SyncEngine.start() re-resolves the principal after the credential fetch and transport connect, before the handshake; if it changed it disconnects and starts over (at most 2 restarts, then PRINCIPAL_CHANGED). The session's principal (sessionPrincipal) is what an accepted handshake binds. Store bindings are serialized (withPrincipalLock). Tests: sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-52), kora auth-sync-coordinator.test.ts, packages/test/tests/phase2-held-writes.test.ts (RT-52). Residual: a write in the same tick as the auth event, before the async binding completes, is still authored under the previous user's node (documented).

problems.title: A parked adoption (RT-46) is retried only at a session start or after the open tab's own uploads progress: an idle connected tab never retries a closed tab's deferred writes, however long ago the park expired
problems.notes: Phase 2 red-team review round 3, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase2.md, Round 3). Liveness. Locations: sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:3927 maybeYieldToDeferredNode (requires sessionAcked > 0 and is only reached from maybeEndSessionForNodeWork after an ack, :3892); :3665 parkAdoption (untilMs is never armed as a timer). A closed tab's write deferred once (retriable) is parked for 30 s; the open tab reconnects as its own node and stays connected and idle (dashboard, kiosk, tab left open): the write is never retried while the connection holds (reported as pending, but it lives only on this device). Required fix: arm a timer for the earliest parked untilMs (and for causal deferrals) that ends an idle own-node session, or upload parked nodes on a side session; keep the bound of one retry per backoff. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-53.test.ts (36 s real wait). FIXED (sync): an own-node session arms a timer for the earliest parked adoption's untilMs; when it fires on an idle session (nothing queued or in flight) the engine reconnects and the next session adopts the node; a busy session hands over when its uploads drain (an expired park is due without own progress). One retry per backoff kept. Timer cleared with the session. TestDevice gains an opt-in reconnectable transport; the repro runs on fake timers (Date + setTimeout, advancing with real time) instead of a 36 s wait. Tests: sync local-nodes.test.ts (RT-53).

problems.title: Merged server fold passed authoritativeNodeIds as an array where the core fold calls Set.has (every server-authored write to a merge('server-authoritative') field throws), and the handshake's authoritativeNodeIds came from a second source (a KoraSyncServerConfig option defaulting to [store node, 'kora:scope-entry']) instead of the list the stores fold with
problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02. Also build breakage of the merge: Operation.foldState declared twice (core), two Store.loadAuthoritativeNodeIds under two meta keys (store), KoraSyncServer.authoritativeNodeIds declared as field and getter (server). Fixed: ServerFoldOptions = FoldOptions with a Set; one persisted list (sync_authoritative_node_ids) feeds the client fold and the sync engine; KoraSyncServer.authoritativeNodeIds = ServerStore.getAuthoritativeNodeIds() (store node id, which authors route writes, side effects and corrections, plus configured extras) is what every session advertises; the separate server option is removed. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-54.test.ts (= tests/server-authoritative-convergence.test.ts: a server-authoritative field converges identically on server and devices through memory, SQLite and Postgres stores; handshake list == stores list).

problems.title: A scope retraction quarantines (and since W7 B1 excludes from the fold) an own write already on the wire; the server stores it, so the device diverges from every other replica (RT-27 retract case regressed)

tests.title: a device regaining scope after a retraction keeps its newer offline edit

problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02. Location: sync/src/engine/outbound-queue.ts rejectRecord took in-flight (sent) operations; sync-engine applyScopeRetraction recorded them as terminal SCOPE_RETRACTED, which B1 excludes from the fold. Fixed: rejectRecord never takes an operation already put on the wire; its ack (stored) or rejection resolves it. Unit test sync outbound-queue.test.ts.

problems.title: SQLite and Postgres server stores drop the protocol v2 encryption envelope: a relayed encrypted op has no ciphertext and every receiving device quarantines it (encrypted sync through a SQL store never works)
problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02. Fixed: operations.encrypted (JSON, verbatim) on SQLite and Postgres next to hash_version (both migrate with ADD COLUMN), deserialized back onto op.encrypted; an unreadable envelope column throws so the startup integrity scan quarantines the row. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-56.test.ts (= tests/encryption-server-stores.test.ts: two encrypted devices through memory, SQLite and Postgres stores; stored ops keep envelope and hashVersion 2, verify after decryption, the server never materializes sealed values, nothing quarantined).

problems.title: Encrypted devices quarantine every server-authored plaintext operation (cascades, set-nulls, constraint corrections, route writes) as PLAINTEXT_REJECTED: the server has no key, so its side effects never reach encrypted devices
problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02. Fixed: the sync engine accepts a plaintext operation from a node the handshake named authoritative when it touches only the collection's cleartextFields (SyncEncryptor.isCleartextOnly; a delete carries no fields); a server write to a sealed field is still refused. Scope entries (kora:scope-entry) restate sealed fields as null and stay refused under encryption (documented limitation). Repro RT-57.test.ts (the cascade step of the encrypted e2e); unit tests sync-encryptor.test.ts.

problems.title: Server fold ignores envelope operations with data null (no cleartext field): a sealed insert never creates the record and a sealed update does not count against a delete, so the server's record existence (scopes, cascades, cross-record rules) disagrees with the devices
problems.acceptanceTest: packages/core/src/fold/fold.test.ts (sealed envelope operations: insert creates the record, a later sealed update revives, cleartext fields fold) + packages/test/tests/encryption-server-stores.test.ts (sealed-only collection)
problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02. Fixed in core mergeOp: an operation carrying op.encrypted with data null sets the record's creation stamp (insert) and write stamp; sealed values are never materialized.

problems.title: Renumbering a version-2 op (SEQUENCE_CONFLICT, RT-35) gives it a new id but leaves later ops naming the old id in causalDeps; the W6 legacy repair could re-hash a server-stored version-2 op, which would then be stored a second time (atomic increments applied twice)
problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02.
