Fixed: Store.resequenceOperation rewrites never-sent dependents (re-hashed, transitively) in the same transaction and returns them; the engine passes its unsent queued ops and swaps them in the queue and own-ack tracking; already-sent dependents keep their ids and replayTo resolves the old id through _kora_seq_conflicts.reemitted_as; the W6 repair renumbers the version-1 half of a mixed pair (id kept, deduplicated by the server). Invariant review (RT-31/32/35/36/43/44) in the seam report. Repro RT-59.test.ts (= tests/renumber-v2-chain.test.ts: 3-op chain insert + 2 increments, first op renumbered, dependents unsent and already stored); unit tests store local-sync-records.test.ts, sequence-repair.test.ts.

problems.title: A device applying a remote delete cascades with operations stamped at its own current time: if it applies the delete after another device's later edit or re-point of the child, its cascade erases that edit on every replica (the server's own copy, stamped right after the delete, would not)
problems.notes: Phase 3 seam review (B1 client fold x B2 server fold x B3 protocol v2), 2026-10-02. B1 residual (client cascades of remote deletes vs server/ cascades). Fixed: kora apply-pipeline stamps a remote delete's side effects with a clock seeded at the delete's HLC (next logical ticks on this node), like timestampAfter on the server; Store.createMutationContext accepts a clock. All copies are idempotent in effect and a later write wins everywhere. Repro RT-60.test.ts (= tests/client-cascade-convergence.test.ts, 3 devices, cascade and set-null).

problems.title: A device can hand-shake with the server's own node id (published in the handshake's authoritativeNodeIds) and author merge('server-authoritative') writes: the session reserves only the kora: namespace, and a server node with no stored history has no claim, so the first device to present it claims it
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Security (authority bypass). Locations: server/src/session/client-session.ts:1773 (only the reserved kora: prefix is refused), :1834 (the claim rule refuses a node with stored history and no owner, so the window is a server node with no history yet: a new deployment, or every restart with an auto-generated node id, RT-62); :2075 (the handshake publishes the ids); core/src/fold/fold.ts:183 (classify: class 1 by op.nodeId). The forged node's uploads beat every device write of the field and earlier server decisions, on the server and on every device. Consequences by code reading: on Postgres its sequence numbers also collide with the server's cached reserveSequenceNumber counter (postgres-server-store.ts:208), so later server side effects and corrections are refused with SEQUENCE_CONFLICT; under encryption, plaintext ops from the forged node that touch only cleartext fields are accepted without decryption (sync-engine.ts:2942). Required fix: refuse at handshake any nodeId in ServerStore.getAuthoritativeNodeIds() (and any id the store authors under); pre-claim the server node ids in the node-claims table at startup; refuse uploads whose nodeId is authoritative. Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-61.test.ts. Fixed (commit 371cf12): the handshake refuses (INVALID_NODE_ID, non-retriable) any kora: node id, the store's node id and every advertised authoritative id, current or legacy, whether or not it has history; uploads are re-checked (checkUploadIntegrity). Server node ids are kora:server:<deployment>:<instance> (RT-62), so a device can never claim one. HTTP long-poll sessions keep the final queued error pollable after the close. Tests: src/session/server-node-identity.test.ts (memory, WebSocket, HTTP). Repro adapted: the configured 'server-1' is now a legacy authoritative id; both it and the current id are refused.

problems.title: Server node ids are auto-generated per process by default (memory, SQLite, Postgres stores): every restart advertises a new authoritativeNodeIds list, devices replace their persisted list and re-fold, demoting every earlier server write of a merge('server-authoritative') field while the server's fold states keep its class; instances on one Postgres database each advertise only their own random id, and configuring one shared id instead makes the instances collide on the server node's sequence numbers
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Convergence. Locations: server/src/store/memory-server-store.ts:135, sqlite-server-store.ts:157, postgres-server-store.ts:180 (nodeId ?? generateUUIDv7(), never persisted); docs/guide/storage-configuration.md:119 ('Usually left to auto-generate'); store/src/store/store.ts:998 (setAuthoritativeNodeIds replaces the set and re-folds); server/src/store/record-fold.ts foldPlanFingerprint (does not cover the authoritative ids, so server states are never re-folded); postgres-server-store.ts:208 (reserveSequenceNumber caches a per-instance counter). Repro 1 (packages/test, SQLite file store restarted): the server keeps 'approved', the old device and a new device show the device's later 'client'. Repro 2 (packages/server, Postgres, two instances with one configured nodeId): the second instance's route writes are refused with SEQUENCE_CONFLICT. Consequences by code reading: encrypted devices quarantine (PLAINTEXT_REJECTED) every plaintext server op of an earlier process (cascades, set-nulls, corrections), because the cleartext exemption keys on the current list; a compacted client base keeps the old classes, so compacted and uncompacted records disagree after the switch. Required fix: persist the server node id in the database (kora_server_meta) on first start and share it across instances; allocate server sequence numbers from the database (under the delivery-counter lock), not a per-process counter; make authority stable (devices union, never drop, ids they learned, or authority is recorded with the persisted server id list); include the authoritative set in the fold plan fingerprint on both sides. Fixed (commit 371cf12): persisted deployment identity in kora_server_meta (server_deployment_id, server_derivation_secret); node id kora:server:<deploymentId>:<instanceId>; SQLite persists its instance id, Postgres draws one per start from server_instance_counter (or a configured instanceId), so instances never share (node, seq). Authority = prefix rule (ServerAuthoritySet) + explicit legacy ids; at the first start of this release the ids whose ops hold class 1 in stored fold states, and a configured plain nodeId, are persisted as server_legacy_authoritative_node_ids and advertised. The fold plan fingerprint covers the explicit authorities. Client half (prefix rule in core fold, union of learned ids) is owned by the other Phase 3 engineer. Repros: RT-62.test.ts (restart keeps the same authoritativeNodeIds; assertion inverted from 'a new random id') and RT-62-shared-node.test.ts (adapted: two instances, distinct instance ids in one deployment, server-authoritative writes from both beat a later device write). Tests: src/store/server-identity.test.ts.

problems.title: The client fold has no plan fingerprint: after a schema change of a field's fold kind (number -> merge('counter'), array -> append-only, a field gaining a resolver), every existing record keeps a fold state of the old kind and mergeOp throws FoldStateError for every later write to that field: local writes fail, and a remote op touching it stalls the device's delivery stream
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Locations: core/src/fold/fold.ts:150 and :412 (fieldPlanFor throws), store/src/store/store.ts:960 (ensureMaterialization re-materializes once per database: fold_materialization = fold-v1, no plan fingerprint); sync/src/engine/sync-engine.ts:2831 (an apply error other than REFERENTIAL_INTEGRITY stalls the watermark, so the device stops applying everything after it; by code reading). The server re-folds on a plan change (record-fold.ts foldPlanFingerprint), so the server keeps working and devices diverge. A changed resolver source is not detected on devices either. Required fix: persist the client's fold plan fingerprint (same definition as the server's) and re-fold affected records on open when it changes; treat FoldStateError on apply as a re-fold of that record, never a stall. Repro kora/tests/repro/RT-63.test.ts.

problems.title: A protocol-2 client can omit hashVersion: version-1 ids are verified nowhere (server or clients) and stores deduplicate by id alone, so a writer can pre-store an arbitrary operation under a predictable server-derived id (cascade-late, constraint corrections) and the server's later correction is dropped as a duplicate
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Integrity bypass. Locations: server/src/session/client-session.ts:2689 (only a declared version 2 is verified), sync/src/engine/verify-inbound.ts:53 (clients skip version 1), server/src/store/memory-server-store.ts:182 (dedup by id; SQLite and Postgres the same); server/src/constraints/constraint-authority.ts:337 (cascade-late parent key = parent delete id | child newest op id, both known to the writer) and :196 (unique/capacity correction parent = hlc:<losing write's HLC>, chosen by the writer). Repro: a comment written under an already deleted cascade parent survives on the server (control without the squat op: deleted). The same squat keeps a losing unique/capacity write (by code reading). Required fix: a protocol-2 session must declare hashVersion 2 on every op and pass verification (version 1 only from protocol-1 sessions); verify version-1 ids too (they cover type, collection, recordId, data, timestamp, nodeId); never let a client op occupy an id the server derives (dedup server-derived ops by (nodeId, id), or refuse a client op whose id is a derived id). Fixed (commit 371cf12): the server verifies every plaintext upload id; an op without hashVersion is verified as a version-1 hash (binary values accepted in bytes or $koraBytes form) and stored declaring hashVersion 1; verify-inbound verifies declared version-1 ops on clients (absent = unverified: pre-beta.14 rows, server transforms, protocol-1 encrypted payloads; kora:* nodes exempt). Server-derived ids are HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the persisted deployment secret (deriveServerOpId), deterministic across instances. Repro strengthened: honest ops carry real ids, the squat is refused INVALID_OPERATION_ID and the late child is deleted. Test helpers now build real content-addressed ids.

problems.title: The Postgres server store cannot store a string containing U+0000 or a lone UTF-16 surrogate: a NUL from ordinary user input drops the session on every upload, so the device re-sends it forever and every later write of that device never reaches anyone; a lone surrogate reaches peers corrupted (U+FFFD) with no error
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Not a Phase 3 regression (first found here). Locations: server/src/store/materialization.ts:37-41 (arrays, objects and json materialize as JSONB, which refuses \u0000 and unpaired surrogate escapes), postgres-server-store.ts collection rows (TEXT refuses NUL). The SQLite and memory server stores and every client store keep both values. Repro packages/test/tests/repro/RT-65.test.ts (KORA_PG_TEST_URL; NUL in a string, lone surrogate in a string, NUL in an array element): the NUL cases never deliver the device's later ordinary write (the client only sees 'server disconnected', repeatedly); the surrogate case delivers the title with replacement characters to the peer. Required fix: one value encoding at the Postgres boundary that round-trips every JS string (escape NUL and lone surrogates in TEXT/JSONB, or keep materialized JSON in TEXT), and a non-retriable, surfaced refusal for anything a store still cannot hold (never a session drop that loops). Server half fixed (commit b53ab47): text codec (U+FFFF-introduced escapes) for Postgres TEXT/JSONB and SQLite TEXT raw-string columns, per-table migration of legacy U+FFFF values, identifiers with NUL/lone surrogates refused (INVALID_IDENTIFIER), database value refusals mapped to non-retriable UNSTORABLE_VALUE (never a dropped session). Parity test src/store/string-fidelity.test.ts (memory/SQLite/Postgres). Repro: both NUL cases pass; the lone-surrogate case still fails because the CLIENT SQLite store (packages/store, better-sqlite3 UTF-8 binding) turns a lone surrogate into U+FFFD on the writing device and the peer (the server now holds and relays it intact). Remaining: the client store codec (store owner).

problems.title: A replace-mode restore of a compacted device's backup on another device rebuilds records from an incomplete log: the backup carries no fold base states, the restoring device clears its own, and it judges the log clean from its own meta (never compacted; gaps checked only for its own nodes), so records whose insert was compacted disappear and fields whose last write was compacted revert
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Locations: store/src/backup/restore.ts:126-133 (fold state and base tables deleted), backup.ts (no _kora_fold_base, _kora_compacted_through or compaction marker exported), store/src/store/store.ts:2502-2509 (ensureMaterialization after the restore) with log-integrity/log-integrity.ts:229-231 (gaps for local nodes only; compactedAt from the restoring device's meta) and store.ts:965-970 (mode 'log'). The backup's own rows are overwritten by the rebuild. A synced device gets the records back on its full resync (the restore resets delivery to 0); a device that restores while offline, or a restore used for disaster recovery, keeps the loss. Required fix: export and import the fold base states (or never compact what a backup cannot carry); at least treat a restored log as 'snapshot+log' when the backup's manifest says its source compacted.

problems.title: The fold voids the per-field versions of a scope-entry insert that carries no fold state: fieldWriteStamp takes max(fieldVersion, op stamp) and the op is stamped at the record's latest version, so every restated field is written at the latest write of any field and beats a device's concurrent offline edit (beta.13 servers, stores without fold state, an unreadable carried state)
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Mixed versions / fallback path. Locations: core/src/fold/fold.ts:164-177 (fieldWriteStamp), server/src/session/client-session.ts:3375 (timestamp = fieldVersions.latest; the beta.13 server does the same), fold.ts:196-207 (an unreadable foldState, e.g. another FOLD_STATE_VERSION, falls back to this path). The device keeps the restated old value while the server folds the device's upload: permanent divergence on that device. beta.13 devices honoured the per-field versions (resolvePerFieldLww). Required fix: stamp each restated field at exactly its own version and never raise it to the op's stamp; for a field without a version use the record's creation version.

problems.title: Row-based base snapshots (client 'snapshot+log' after a pre-W7 compaction; client 'kept' when the log has ANY quarantined row, which turns every record of the database into a snapshot) drop every late concurrent write older than a field's version: counter deltas, array adds and richtext updates that every other replica folds
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). The documented 'approximate' path, constructed: device c held insert + restock (stock 15, tags [x, y]); an offline device's older write (stock -1, tag z) arrives later; every replica folds stock 14 and tags [x, z, y], the snapshot replica keeps 15 and [x, y] for good. Snapshot stamps also carry no authority class, so a server-authoritative value whose winning server write is older than a losing device write flips when that device write is merged again (by code reading). Also reached on a FOLD_STATE_VERSION bump with a compacted log (old base states become unreadable and are replaced by row snapshots). Locations: core/src/fold/snapshot.ts:110-137, store/src/fold/rematerialize.ts:84-96, store/src/store/store.ts:965-970. Required fix: re-bootstrap such records from the server's fold state (a scope entry carries foldState) instead of folding against a row snapshot; for 'kept', snapshot only the records that own a quarantined row, not the whole database.

problems.title: Every device that applies a remote cascading delete authors, stores and uploads its own copy of every cascade/set-null (own node, own id): deleting a parent with N children stores about N x (devices + 2) child deletes, relayed to every device, and every device that later syncs from scratch adds N more
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Write amplification, unbounded in the number of devices over time. Location: kora/src/apply-pipeline.ts:301-320 (applySideEffectOps writes through createMutationContext, so the copies queue for sync). Repro: 4 devices, 20 children: 100 task deletes stored (author 20, server 20, three receivers 60); a fifth device syncing afterwards added 20 more. Copies from users without write grants on the children are refused and recorded as terminal rejections. Required fix: a receiving device's cascades of a REMOTE delete stay local (fold them without enqueuing: the author uploaded its copy and the server derives its own), or give them an id and content every device derives identically so the log stores one.

problems.title: Server stores with an unclean log (quarantined rows) keep pre-fold rows at the upgrade, but the next write to such a record re-folds it from the remaining log: the quarantined operation's effect vanishes, and a record whose insert was quarantined disappears from the server
problems.notes: Phase 3 red-team review, 2026-10-02 (remediation/evidence/redteam-phase3.md). Locations: server/src/store/sqlite-server-store.ts:1214-1217 (skippedUnclean leaves no fold state); the next apply takes the 'no state' path and re-folds from the log (Postgres the same). The console message promises the rows 'keep their pre-fold values until their next write'; that next write is what drops them, and new devices then enter scope without the record. Required fix: on the unclean path build the record's base from its kept row and fold later writes onto it (with RT-68's caveats), or refuse writes to records with quarantined history until an operator repairs them. Repro packages/server/tests/repro/RT-70.test.ts (SQLite). Fixed (commit b53ab47): records that own quarantined rows (from operations_quarantine.row_json; an unreadable collection/record widens the scope) are never re-folded from their incomplete log: the startup migration, the next write and reads rebuild them from the stored fold state or a createSnapshotState base of the kept row (fields stamped at least at the quarantined ops' newest HLC) with the remaining ops merged on top; records whose every op was quarantined get a state too; complete records fold from their log. SQLite and Postgres. Inverted the fold-materialization test that encoded the bug. Tests: tests/integration/quarantine-base.test.ts.
